_note: Research candidate locations (descriptions from the project proposal). Contains NO measurements: terrain values come only from processed datasets. 'tiles' lists the connected elevation tiles for each site.

sites.name: Atacama Desert
sites.description: One of the driest non-polar places on Earth. The connected tile spans the Calama basin, the Cordillera de la Sal near Valle de la Luna, and Andean volcanoes to the north-east.
sites.potential_comparison: Selected arid and rocky Martian environments; slope and relief analogs for lunar terrain
sites.caution: Aridity does not reproduce Mars's atmosphere, radiation or temperature; the Moon's environment differs even more.

sites.name: Death Valley
sites.description: Deep desert basin with salt pans, alluvial fans, dunes and steep surrounding ranges.
sites.caution: Terrain varies strongly across the region; results depend on the exact analysis window.

sites.name: Meteor Crater
sites.description: Well-preserved simple impact crater about 1.2 km across on the Colorado Plateau.
sites.potential_comparison: Impact-crater landforms on the Moon and Mars
sites.caution: A terrestrial impact structure has a different erosion and geological history.

sites.name: Hawaiian volcanic fields
sites.description: Basaltic lava flows, cinder cones and tephra on the upper slopes of Mauna Kea and Mauna Loa.
sites.caution: Basalt alone does not establish full material equivalence.

sites.name: Icelandic volcanic landscapes
sites.description: Young lava fields and volcanic sand plains in the highlands north of Vatnajökull.
sites.caution: Weather, vegetation, ice and seasonal conditions differ markedly.
sites.suggested_tile: ArcticDEM or Copernicus DEM (NASADEM stops at 60° N)
